source.name: Charlotte's Web excerpt — user-supplied targeted items

candidates.contextualMeaning: to never become successful, important, or worthwhile

senseEvidence.sentence: It’s very small and weak, and it will never amount to anything.
senseEvidence.explanation: The speaker predicts that something will never develop into anything valuable.

occurrences.sentence: It’s very small and weak, and it will never amount to anything.

candidates.contextualMeaning: to kill or get rid of it

senseEvidence.sentence: So your father has decided to do away with it.
senseEvidence.explanation: A euphemistic way to say that the pig will be killed.

occurrences.sentence: So your father has decided to do away with it.

candidates.contextualMeaning: cried out in a sudden, high-pitched voice

senseEvidence.sentence: “Do away with it?” shrieked Fern.
senseEvidence.explanation: A sharp, high cry caused by shock and horror.

occurrences.sentence: “Do away with it?” shrieked Fern.

candidates.contextualMeaning: placed a large serving jug on a surface

senseEvidence.sentence: Mrs Arable put a pitcher of cream on the table.
senseEvidence.explanation: The action of setting a serving container down on the table.

occurrences.sentence: Mrs Arable put a pitcher of cream on the table.

candidates.contextualMeaning: spoke or cried while taking broken, tearful breaths

senseEvidence.sentence: “Please don’t kill it!” she sobbed.
senseEvidence.explanation: Crying so strongly that breathing and speech become broken.

occurrences.sentence: “Please don’t kill it!” she sobbed.

candidates.contextualMeaning: a situation where someone’s survival or death is at stake

senseEvidence.sentence: “This is a matter of life and death, and you talk about controlling myself.”
senseEvidence.explanation: An extremely serious situation involving survival.

occurrences.sentence: “This is a matter of life and death, and you talk about controlling myself.”

candidates.contextualMeaning: a person or animal that is physically weak

senseEvidence.sentence: A weakling makes trouble.
senseEvidence.explanation: A dismissive label for the smallest, weakest pig.

occurrences.sentence: A weakling makes trouble.

candidates.contextualMeaning: extremely bad, distressing, or unjust

senseEvidence.sentence: “This is the most terrible case of injustice I ever heard of.”
senseEvidence.explanation: It intensifies Fern’s judgment that the injustice is extremely bad.

occurrences.sentence: “This is the most terrible case of injustice I ever heard of.”

candidates.contextualMeaning: a strange or unusual facial expression

senseEvidence.sentence: A queer look came over John Arable’s face.
senseEvidence.explanation: An old-fashioned expression for a noticeably strange facial expression.

occurrences.sentence: A queer look came over John Arable’s face.

candidates.contextualMeaning: making a repeated scraping sound with claws or feet

senseEvidence.sentence: As she approached her chair, the carton wobbled, and there was a scratching noise.
senseEvidence.explanation: A scraping noise made by the pig moving inside the carton.

occurrences.sentence: As she approached her chair, the carton wobbled, and there was a scratching noise.

candidates.contextualMeaning: happening earlier than expected or at an tragically inappropriate time

senseEvidence.sentence: “Saved from an untimely death.”
senseEvidence.explanation: The pig’s death would have occurred tragically early in its life.

occurrences.sentence: “Saved from an untimely death.”

candidates.contextualMeaning: pitifully small, weak, or poor in condition

senseEvidence.sentence: “You call that miserable thing a pig?”
senseEvidence.explanation: Avery uses it contemptuously to describe the weak pig as pathetic.

occurrences.sentence: “You call that miserable thing a pig?”

candidates.contextualMeaning: an individual example of a particular type of animal or thing

senseEvidence.sentence: “That’s a fine specimen of a pig – it’s no bigger than a white rat.”
senseEvidence.explanation: One animal considered as an example of its species.

occurrences.sentence: “That’s a fine specimen of a pig – it’s no bigger than a white rat.”

candidates.contextualMeaning: to give items to different people according to a rule

senseEvidence.sentence: “No, I only distribute pigs to early risers,” said Mr Arable.
senseEvidence.explanation: Mr Arable humorously describes giving pigs to selected recipients.

occurrences.sentence: “No, I only distribute pigs to early risers,” said Mr Arable.

candidates.contextualMeaning: in spite of the fact just mentioned

senseEvidence.sentence: “A small one, to be sure, but nevertheless a pig.”
senseEvidence.explanation: It contrasts the pig’s small size with the fact that it is still truly a pig.

occurrences.sentence: “A small one, to be sure, but nevertheless a pig.”

candidates.contextualMeaning: a very young baby or newborn animal

senseEvidence.sentence: A minute later, Fern was seated on the floor in the corner of the kitchen with her infant between her knees, teaching it to suck from the bottle.
senseEvidence.explanation: The newborn pig is treated like a human baby.

occurrences.sentence: A minute later, Fern was seated on the floor in the corner of the kitchen with her infant between her knees, teaching it to suck from the bottle.

candidates.contextualMeaning: the natural desire to eat food

senseEvidence.sentence: The pig, although tiny, had a good appetite and caught on quickly.
senseEvidence.explanation: The pig is eager and able to consume milk.

occurrences.sentence: The pig, although tiny, had a good appetite and caught on quickly.

candidates.contextualMeaning: gave an order firmly and authoritatively

senseEvidence.sentence: “Run!” commanded Mrs Arable, taking the pig from Fern and slipping a doughnut into her hand.
senseEvidence.explanation: Mrs Arable gives Fern an urgent, direct order.

occurrences.sentence: “Run!” commanded Mrs Arable, taking the pig from Fern and slipping a doughnut into her hand.

candidates.contextualMeaning: quickly and smoothly putting something into a place or someone’s hand

senseEvidence.sentence: “Run!” commanded Mrs Arable, taking the pig from Fern and slipping a doughnut into her hand.
senseEvidence.explanation: A quick, unobtrusive action of putting the doughnut into Fern’s hand.

occurrences.sentence: “Run!” commanded Mrs Arable, taking the pig from Fern and slipping a doughnut into her hand.

candidates.contextualMeaning: went up and entered by stepping upward

senseEvidence.sentence: The children ran out to the road and climbed into the bus.
senseEvidence.explanation: The children step up into the school bus.

occurrences.sentence: The children ran out to the road and climbed into the bus.

candidates.contextualMeaning: extremely happy, peaceful, and satisfying

senseEvidence.sentence: She just sat and stared out of the window, thinking what a blissful world it was and how lucky she was to have entire charge of a pig.
senseEvidence.explanation: Fern sees the world as perfectly happy because the pig has been saved.

occurrences.sentence: She just sat and stared out of the window, thinking what a blissful world it was and how lucky she was to have entire charge of a pig.

candidates.contextualMeaning: to look upward steadily and with admiration or affection

senseEvidence.sentence: He would stand and gaze up at her with adoring eyes.
senseEvidence.explanation: Wilbur looks steadily upward at Fern with affection.

occurrences.sentence: He would stand and gaze up at her with adoring eyes.

candidates.contextualMeaning: a small building or room used for storing firewood

senseEvidence.sentence: Then, when Mrs Arable complained, he was moved to a bigger box in the woodshed.
senseEvidence.explanation: The outbuilding where Wilbur’s larger box is kept.

occurrences.sentence: Then, when Mrs Arable complained, he was moved to a bigger box in the woodshed.

candidates.contextualMeaning: the season when apple trees are flowering

senseEvidence.sentence: It was apple-blossom time, and the days were getting warmer.
senseEvidence.explanation: A seasonal description locating the event in spring.

occurrences.sentence: It was apple-blossom time, and the days were getting warmer.

candidates.contextualMeaning: made a short, low, rough sound like a pig

senseEvidence.sentence: When he had finished the last drop, he grunted and walked sleepily into the box.
senseEvidence.explanation: The pig makes its characteristic low sound after feeding.

occurrences.sentence: When he had finished the last drop, he grunted and walked sleepily into the box.

candidates.contextualMeaning: looked carefully through a narrow opening because seeing was difficult

senseEvidence.sentence: Fern peered through the door.
senseEvidence.explanation: Fern looks intently through the small doorway to see Wilbur inside.

occurrences.sentence: Fern peered through the door.

candidates.contextualMeaning: moved forward close to the ground on the body or short legs

senseEvidence.sentence: He crawled into the tunnel and disappeared from sight, completely covered with straw.
senseEvidence.explanation: Wilbur moves low into the straw tunnel.

occurrences.sentence: He crawled into the tunnel and disappeared from sight, completely covered with straw.

candidates.contextualMeaning: filled with delight and fascination

senseEvidence.sentence: Fern was enchanted.
senseEvidence.explanation: Fern is charmed and delighted by Wilbur’s clever nesting behavior.

occurrences.sentence: Fern was enchanted.

candidates.contextualMeaning: walked through water that was not deep

senseEvidence.sentence: When she waded into the brook, Wilbur waded in with her.
senseEvidence.explanation: Wilbur walks through the shallow brook rather than swimming.

occurrences.sentence: When she waded into the brook, Wilbur waded in with her.

candidates.contextualMeaning: kept oneself pleasantly occupied or entertained

senseEvidence.sentence: Wilbur amused himself in the mud along the edge of the brook, where it was warm and moist and delightfully sticky and oozy.
senseEvidence.explanation: Wilbur entertains himself by playing in the warm mud.

occurrences.sentence: Wilbur amused himself in the mud along the edge of the brook, where it was warm and moist and delightfully sticky and oozy.

candidates.contextualMeaning: in a way that gives great pleasure or enjoyment

senseEvidence.sentence: Wilbur amused himself in the mud along the edge of the brook, where it was warm and moist and delightfully sticky and oozy.
senseEvidence.explanation: It positively intensifies how enjoyable the sticky mud feels to Wilbur.

occurrences.sentence: Wilbur amused himself in the mud along the edge of the brook, where it was warm and moist and delightfully sticky and oozy.

candidates.contextualMeaning: soft, wet, and slowly flowing like thick mud

senseEvidence.sentence: Wilbur amused himself in the mud along the edge of the brook, where it was warm and moist and delightfully sticky and oozy.
senseEvidence.explanation: The mud is thick, wet, and pleasantly squishy.

occurrences.sentence: Wilbur amused himself in the mud along the edge of the brook, where it was warm and moist and delightfully sticky and oozy.

candidates.contextualMeaning: animal waste used as fertilizer for soil

senseEvidence.sentence: Next day Wilbur was taken from his home under the apple tree and went to live in a manure pile in the cellar of Zuckerman’s barn.
senseEvidence.explanation: The animal-waste pile in the barn cellar where Wilbur is housed.

occurrences.sentence: Next day Wilbur was taken from his home under the apple tree and went to live in a manure pile in the cellar of Zuckerman’s barn.
